home.title: Find out your HIV risk in about 1 minute
home.intro: Answer 9 simple questions about your life and habits. We will show your risk level, what is raising it, and what you can do next.
steps: See your risk level: Low, Medium or High
Get simple advice on what to do next
home.privacy: No name, phone number or login. Your answers cannot be traced back to you.
home.disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not an HIV test. Only a test at a health centre can tell your HIV status.

low.name: Low risk
low.desc: Your answers show a lower chance of HIV exposure. Keep protecting yourself.

medium.desc: Some of your habits increase your chance of HIV exposure. A test is a good idea.

tips.std: Get checked and treated for STIs at a health centre. Untreated STIs make HIV much easier to catch.
tips.tested_past_year: Get an HIV test at least once a year. It is free at most health centres and takes about 20 minutes.
tips.aids_education: Learn the basics: how HIV spreads, how condoms protect you, and how PrEP and PEP work. Ask at any health centre.
tips.place: Partners met this way are linked to higher HIV risk. Always use condoms and ask a health worker about PrEP.
tips.background: This is part of your background and cannot be changed, but it means regular testing and condoms matter even more for you.

low: Get an HIV test once a year to stay sure.
Share what you know about HIV with friends.
medium: Get an HIV test in the next few weeks.
Use condoms every time you have sex.
Ask a health worker if PrEP is right for you.
high: Get an HIV test as soon as possible. It is free and confidential.
Ask a health worker about PrEP, a daily pill that prevents HIV.
If you had risky sex in the last 3 days, ask for PEP urgently.
Use condoms every time you have sex.

whatif.title: What if things changed?
whatif.intro: Change your answers below to see how your risk level would change. Nothing here is saved.

sections.p: This tool estimates how vulnerable a person may be to HIV based on everyday behaviours and background, such as where they meet partners, past STIs, testing habits and age. It helps people notice their risk early and get tested.

A machine learning model was trained on survey answers from about 700 people with known HIV test results. It looks at how your answers combine, not just at one answer, to give a Low, Medium or High risk level.
It cannot tell whether you have HIV. It can be wrong. It was trained on a small dataset that may not represent your community. Always confirm with an HIV test at a health centre.

In the data used to train the model, drug use did not show the increased risk that health research expects. Because of this, the tool never gives advice based on drug use. Sharing needles and drug use do increase HIV risk in real life.
We never ask for your name, phone number or location. We only keep anonymous answers (without your exact age or sexual attraction) to understand how many people are at risk.
